title: Strictly Increasing Dice
problem: Three fair six-sided dice are rolled in order. What is the probability that the first result is strictly less than the second, and the second is strictly less than the third?

hints.text: A strictly increasing result must use three different face values.
Choose three values from the six. For each chosen set, exactly one of its six orderings is increasing.

solution.setup: There are 6^3 equally likely ordered triples of die results.
solution.reasoning: Choose the three distinct face values used by the triple. There are C(6,3)=20 choices. Once the values are chosen, exactly one ordering places them in strictly increasing order, so there are 20 favorable ordered triples out of 216.
solution.sanityCheck: Conditional on three distinct results, all six relative orders are symmetric and only one is increasing. Since ties are possible, the unconditional probability must be below 1/6; 5/54 is about 9.3%.

keyInsight: Choose the distinct values first, then use the unique order satisfying the strict inequality.
recognitionCues: A strict ordering condition implies distinct values and makes relative-order symmetry useful.
commonMistakes: Answering 1/6 without accounting for rolls containing ties.
followUps: What is the probability that the results are nondecreasing rather than strictly increasing?

source.notes: Original formulation of a standard ordered-dice family.
